title: Microsoft Copilot: Copilot Code builds software and apps from plain-language descriptions
summary: Hold: the spending-policy and Intune paths omit navigation needed to reach the controls. The Graph endpoint and its named properties are documented, but its partial body should be moved into the note and the disabled-on-creation lifecycle made clear. The roadmap facts and documented licensing and billing claims are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management is the complete path to configure who can build and their monthly limit.
claims.quote: Select the **Configuration** tab and then select **+ Add spending policy**. ... Create and name the policy and then choose **Identity** as the scope.
claims.fix: Replace the row's path with 'Copilot > Cost management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Specific groups > Select agents and services > Copilot Code > Set limits and alerts'. The cited licensing page supplies the Code selection; the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits supplies the wizard navigation. Apply the same complete route where the prose gives creation instructions.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies with the listed body properties implements the row's access and monthly-limit control.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... Required properties are `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `serviceSettings`.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies', retaining its docs link. Replace the row note with 'Beta API. The request body sets periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings and requires displayName and a concrete @odata.type. New policies are created disabled; for group-scoped policies, link the audience with Add assigned group and let the service enable the policy once its requirements are satisfied. The example shows serviceId values cowork and workIQ, not one for Copilot Code. Creation also requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.' The endpoint and printed keys are valid; omitted audience and other request details are left to the reference, not treated as an invalid call.

claims.claim: The spending-policy API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.quote: "serviceSettings": [ { "serviceId": "cowork", "state": "enabled" }, { "serviceId": "workIQ", "state": "enabled" } ]

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy through Graph requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: In Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Copilot > Code Tab is a complete route from the admin centre to the sandbox policies.
claims.quote: Select **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Configuration** > **Create** > **New policy**. ... **Profile type**: Select **Templates** > **Imported Administrative templates (Preview)**
claims.fix: Replace the Intune path with 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Windows 10 and later > Templates > Imported Administrative templates (Preview) > Create > Configuration settings > Microsoft Copilot > Code Tab'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/import-custom-admx-templates to sources for the route into the imported-template profile. Keep the existing code-admin docs link for the policy's own location, and state that the Microsoft Copilot ADMX/ADML templates must first be imported.
